    - You've been out to the Jaw with an old man and brought him home. Sit. Not there. That end.
    - The lee's clear, Kor says. He sat there an hour this morning waiting on a slack. First time in his life.
    - The boy came back. Stood a yard to my left. I said nothing. He said nothing. Good morning, that was.
    - You again. Good.
    - Ask it, then. Before the turn.

    - Varro. Warden fifty-six years. Never lost a ship in the gap. Luck.
    - Knees stopped me five years back. A pilot who can't brace in a cross-sea is no use to anyone, and I said so first. They still bring me the hard questions. I still answer them.
    - That oilskin by my door? Maili's. My wife. She fished the coves, and she handled a boat better than half the wardens. I told her so once. She held it over me thirty years.
    - Fever took her, fourteen years back. I keep the oilskin where I see it going out. That's all. That's enough talking.
    - Iska is the best of them. Don't tell her. Nessa argued every lesson and then did exactly what I said. Still does.
    - Kor goes before slack. One day the tide will tell him what it thinks of that. Corrie writes it all down. She'll be the best of the lot, if Kor doesn't drown her first.
    - The water. Nothing I could put in a book. Or I'm getting old. Ysmay says I've been old for twenty years. She may be right.
    - You saw it with me, out under the Jaw. I had been telling myself it was my eyes. I'd rather have been right about my eyes.
